# GTA VI PC recompilation project shut down by Take-Two

- News
- Entertainment
- Gaming
## GTA VI PC recompilation project shut down by Take-Two

Modders are racing to get Grand Theft Auto VI running on PC.

Modders are racing to get Grand Theft Auto VI running on PC.

Game modding communities are racing to get Grand Theft Auto VI running on PC, but one big effort has been taken down by Take-Two today. Leonida, a fan project by 15-year-old “NotRexed,” has vanished after a DMCA takedown notice from GTA VI publisher Take-Two.

Leonida was designed to translate a leaked GTA VI Xbox build to run natively on Windows. Cyberleek, the leaker who posted multiple GTA VI gameplay videos over the summer, published a full Xbox build of the game earlier this week. The leak has kicked recompilation efforts up a notch, as modders race to reverse-engineer the game’s code and rebuild it into native PC code.

Some have managed to get the game to boot on PC, but recompiling the full game won’t be easy — even with help from AI tools like Claude. Take-Two is trying to slow this progress, and its IP enforcement team targeted the main GitHub repository for Leonida and more than 2,900 forks of it, claiming that it “infringes upon Take-Two’s copyrighted works and facilitates copyright infringement of Rockstar Games title, Grand Theft Auto VI .”

PortWatch VI is tracking the efforts to recompile, emulate, or port the leaked Xbox build over to PC. At the time of publishing, the VIctory project and forks of it are leading the way. People are also trying to use XCL, a compatibility layer that runs Xbox Series X games on a Windows PC, to get GTA VI running.

At this point, it seems like Take-Two might not be able to avoid the inevitable here. The clock started ticking down to the release of the PC version last week, and if recent reports are true, we might see it in a few months. If GTA VI is close to being officially ready for PC, we could hear about a release before modders manage to get the game running on PC unofficially.

- Tom Warren

# Jamaica Suk, producer, DJ, and friend, has died - CDM Create Digital Music

## Jamaica Suk, producer, DJ, and friend, has died

We lost Jamaica Suk yesterday, the singular musical force. To say this hits close to home is an understatement; few people have been a better friend or a greater inspiration. My thoughts are with her family, in particular, right now. Music in the end is just an excuse to spend some time together and share some hopes and dreams. Take care of one another. Here’s the official statement.

> We’re heartbroken to share that we lost Jamaica Suk on Monday, following a battle with an aggressive form of breast cancer. She passed away peacefully in her sleep, with loved ones by her side. No words can make this easier. We all wanted so much more time with Jamaica, and she fought fantastically hard for the past months, care for by her sisters Aysia and Hope. Thank you for your support during this time, when she was unable to work and do what she loved most. Memorial arrangements will be announced soon. We ask for some privacy for the family and friends as everyone processes this enormous loss. Jamaica shared so much love through the music world, from her own Gradient label to a life lived constantly playing — in rock and metal bands, jazz, and techno, across northern California and Berlin and internationally. She was a regular and unforgettable presence at RSO, Radion, Tresor, Melkweg, Basement, Renate, about blank, and many others. She was a long-time resident at Pornceptual, including one Boiler Room stream that was too hot to handle for YouTube. And she was a prolific producer, with a blend of hypnotic, groovy, and hard industrial elements that were instantly recognizable as her personality and warmth. To spend any time with Jamaica was to get to know her dreams, and the fierce tenacity with which she would work to bring them to reality. She literally described dreaming of wires and patch cables. Even in recent days, she was talking about new ideas for music and people she wanted to bring together and show the world. So we ask you to please keep celebrating her music and keep those dreams alive.

The official source for the family and arrangements is @jamaicasuk .

Please, do play some of Jamaica’s music. That remains the answer.

## Retributive Justice

Retributive justice is best understood as the form of justice committed to the following three principles:

- that those who culpably commit certain kinds of wrongful acts, paradigmatically serious crimes, morally deserve to suffer proportionate punishment;
- that it is morally right or intrinsically good—without reference to any further goods that might arise—for some (legitimate) punisher to impose the punishment they deserve; and
- that punishment must not be imposed in the absence of desert or exceed what would be proportional to the wrongful action.
While retributivism was for a long period of time disregarded as “a barbaric remnant of superstitious thought that more rational forms of society would sweep away” (Bennett 2014: 4446), recent work on retributivism has gained much support in the philosophy of punishment, making retributivist views among the dominant candidates for a positive justification of punishment. Still, critics continue to voice the charges of barbarism (Tadros 2011) and moral repugnancy (Scanlon 2008), and many features of retributivism—especially the notions of desert, proportionality, the normative status of suffering, and the ultimate justification for retribution—remain contested. Though theories of retributive justice have ancient and medieval roots, this entry focuses on contemporary conceptions of retributive justice.

## 1. Introducing Retributive Theory

### 1.1 On Punishment

Retributivism offers a justification of punishment. While the definition of punishment is itself a matter of controversy, punishment generally refers to the deliberate or intentional imposition of burdens or suffering on wrongdoers for an act or omission that the punisher believes to be (a culpable) wrong. (The entry on legal punishment discusses this concept in depth.) This definition includes both punishment as it is imposed by the state in the public sphere for the commission of crimes and punitive responses to wrongdoing in other spheres, including the private and the institutional. Still, the challenge of justifying state punishment is the most pressing, as the forms of punishment imposed by the state generally involve sanctions that are different in kind from and more onerous than those imposed outside the political sphere, paradigmatically involving the deprivation of basic human rights (to life, liberty, and property, among others).

Punishment is often analyzed in terms of two constituent parts: censure (or condemnation) and sanction (or hard treatment, that is, treatment that involves a hardship imposed on the person being punished, or at the very least the withdrawal of a benefit to which they would otherwise be entitled).

### 1.2 Basic Strengths and Weaknesses

### 1.2.1 Intuitive Appeal

Many share the intuition that those who commit wrongful acts, especially serious crimes, should be punished even if punishing them would produce no other good (see Darley & Robinson 2002). Consider, for example, being the sentencing judge for an offender who has been convicted of rape. How should you sentence him? You may have the intuition that he should not be “let off easy”. If so, you might think that this reflects the importance of incapacitating him, deterring him and others from future criminal acts, or publicly condemning the crime. But now suppose that he has since suffered an illness that has left him physically incapacitated so that he cannot rape or commit other violent crimes again. Moreover, he has enough money to support himself without resorting to criminal activities. You therefore have no need to take steps to prevent him from committing future crimes. Still, others might be emboldened if you don’t punish him. So suppose further that you could “sentence” him to spend his days on a tropical island of his choosing, where he can relax and enjoy himself, as long as he regularly reports to an island prison to be videoed in prison garb, footage of which is made publicly available, ensuring thereby that others harbor the false belief that he is suffering for his crime. If you believe that this could be done with no prospect of detection, should you choose such a sentence? Many share the intuition that this would be unjust. They believe that the wrongdoing should not go unpunished, even if punishment would achieve no other downstream good (see, e.g., Moore 1997: 98–101).

items.body:
Architecture practice Studio Gang has completed a women's conference centre overlooking Geneva Lake in Wisconsin, with three irregularly shaped buildings informed by the site's oak forest.

Located outside of Chicago on a lakeside hill, the Women's Leadership Center contains meeting spaces for established and emerging women in leadership roles to gather and "ideate solutions to complex issues within their industries".

"Women leaders spend much of their careers in rooms that weren't designed with them in mind," said the center's founder Ann Drake, former CEO of supply chain provider DSC Logistics. "I wanted to build one that was."

Studio Gang said key elements of the design were sustainability – with strategies such as a mass timber structure – and responding to the ecology of the site through gently curving volumes and wide-open windows.

Photographs

Previous

Next

Photographs

Close

"We designed the Women's Leadership Center to respect and learn from its surrounding forest ecology while allowing community, leadership, and collaborative problem-solving to thrive," said Studio Gang founding partner Jeanne Gang.

"Locally sourced materials, mass timber, and low-carbon concrete minimise the buildings' carbon footprint, while the landscape helps to repair the site's ecology and enhance its biodiversity."

Drawings

Previous

Next

Drawings

Close

The campus contains three main buildings -- the circular Council building that functions as the main meeting space, the Lodge, which is made of three interconnected volumes, and the Cabin, a smaller building that contains accommodations.

White oak wood harvested on-site, a dark wood cladding and natural Wisconsin stone were used throughout all three buildings to "reflect the tones and textures of the forest", according to the studio.

The Council building is arranged around a central courtyard and garden that doubles as a rainwater-collection site.

Its rooms, including a larger lecture hall and meeting room, fan outwards around the courtyard and are lined with floor-to-ceiling windows, while a heavy timber structure creates a series of skylights at the entrance.

A walkway leads out the back of the Council building towards the Lodge. The building contains more casual meeting and socialising spaces, such as a Great Room arranged around a fireplace.

It also contains a mass-timber structure above this space, which is lined with skylights. Outdoor terraces overlook Geneva Lake, while the building's green roof contains a "coffee nook" and patios for seating.

Read:

Studio Gang covers theatre for Hudson Valley Shakespeare with mass-timber shell

Tucked off into a corner of the site, the Cabin building contains several bedrooms across two levels, as well as utility spaces such as a laundry room.

Its lower level contains a dining area and living area, which double as additional, more intimate gathering spaces.

Fully accessible ramps interconnect all three structures and lead down to the water bank, where they end in a pier.

Elsewhere, Studio Gang recently completed an open-air theatre in upstate New York and a Denver hotel.

# New Gemini setting lets you keep chat history, but turn off AI training [U]

- Apps & Updates
- Gemini
- Gemini app
## New Gemini setting lets you keep chat history, but turn off AI training [U]

Google is rolling out new privacy settings for the Gemini app that will let you “keep your history while independently controlling generative AI model training.”

Update 11/24 : This new setting is now widely rolling out. On gemini.google.com, tap the settings gear icon to find a new “Gemini History” item at the very bottom. This opens myactivity.google.com/product/gemini with an On/Off dropdown.

Under “Help train generative AI models with,” you’ll find the new “Chat content including text & attachments” setting. It’s enabled by default.

> Your future chats won’t be used to train generative AI models, unless you provide feedback.

Training on “Audio and Gemini Live videos & screenshares” remains an opt-in preference.

Original 11/16 : Gemini’s existing Keep Activity setting “controls how long your chats are saved and whether they are used to train generative AI models.”

Google is now separating that preference into two new options.

## Top comment by Whispy_Snippet

This is huge. One of the major things Siri-AI users on iPhone like to point out is that while their assistant is a less capable portmanteau of Siri and Gemini, their queries are not used for AI training. Gemini on Android, on the other hand, offers the superior AI platform with the caveat that there is no way to opt out of training and still retain your chat history. Until now. Now users of Gemini on Android get the best of both worlds - the best of Google's AI models powering their AI experiences and their chat history siloed from AI training.

Win win.

The first setting is called “History” and lets you “control how long your history is saved.” If disabled:

> “…future chats will be saved for around 2 months and used to respond to you, process your feedback, and protect Google, its users, and the public, with help from human reviewers.”

The duration is currently 24 hours for chat context, and 72 hours to help protect Google, users, and the public.

The second setting allows you to “separately control whether your chat content, including text and attachments, is used to train generative AI models.”

> With this change, you will be able to keep your history while independently controlling generative AI model training.

If Keep Activity is currently off, the two “new settings will both be off.” These changes are rolling out over the “coming weeks,” and Google is notifying users via email.

# USA: US-Gericht spricht Huawei wegen Betrugs schuldig

Huawei: Der chinesische Technologiekonzern wurde vor Gericht schuldig gesprochen. Foto: IMAGO/ZUMA Wire New York. Der chinesische Technologiekonzern Huawei ist in den USA in einem jahrelangen Strafverfahren schuldig gesprochen worden. Eine Jury in Brooklyn befand das Unternehmen am Dienstag in zehn von zwölf Anklagepunkten für schuldig, darunter Bankbetrug, Verstöße gegen Sanktionen und Diebstahl von Geschäftsgeheimnissen.

Die Vorwürfe entbehrten jeder rechtlichen Grundlage, teilte Huawei mit. Man werde rechtliche Schritte einleiten, um die eigenen Rechte zu schützen. Vom Vorwurf der Bildung einer kriminellen Vereinigung sprachen die Geschworenen den Netzwerkausrüster frei.

Die Anklage warf Huawei vor, Banken wie HSBC über Geschäfte im Iran getäuscht zu haben. Meldungen der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters aus den Jahren 2012 und 2013 hatten maßgeblich dazu beigetragen, diese Aktivitäten aufzudecken. Den Geschworenen lag zudem eine Erklärung der Huawei-Finanzchefin Meng Wanzhou vor, in der sie illegale Iran-Geschäfte eingeräumt hatte.

Das Gericht sah es ferner als erwiesen an, dass Huawei über zwei Jahrzehnte hinweg Technologien von US-Firmen wie Cisco und T-Mobile gestohlen hat. Die Verteidigung wies dies zurück: Die Anklage habe sich lediglich unzusammenhängende Vorfälle herausgepickt. Der Erfolg von Huawei beruhe auf eigener Forschung.

items.body:
# Klöckner warnt vor "Wettbewerb der Empörung"

Bundestagspräsidentin Julia Klöckner kritisiert, dass ihrer Ansicht nach in öffentlichen Debatten immer häufiger Empörung statt Argumente zählt. „Wir erleben einen Wettbewerb der Empörung“, sagte die CDU-Politikerin bei einer Feier zum 70-jährigen Bestehen des Deutschen Presserats in Berlin. Soziale Netzwerke verstärkten extreme Positionen, während sachliche Argumente an Bedeutung verlören. Auch in der Politik sei das zu beobachten.

Umso wichtiger sei ein Journalismus, der einordnet, prüft und unterschiedliche Sichtweisen aufzeigt. Gerade durch Künstliche Intelligenz werde es immer schwieriger, verlässliche Informationen von manipulierten Inhalten zu unterscheiden. Journalismus könne dagegen etwas vermitteln, was KI zumindest bei rational denkenden Menschen nicht könne: Vertrauen. Seine Bedeutung werde im KI-Zeitalter deshalb möglicherweise sogar noch größer.

Der Presserat wurde am 20. November 1956 in Bonn gegründet. Er kümmert sich seitdem um die Einhaltung journalistischer Standards und setzt dabei auf freiwillige Selbstkontrolle.

Auch Presseratssprecher Moritz Döbler verwies bei der Jubiläumsfeier auf die Herausforderungen durch KI-generierte Inhalte und die zunehmende Polarisierung in sozialen Medien. „Journalismus funktioniert nur von Mensch zu Mensch“, sagte Döbler, der zugleich Chefredakteur der „Rheinischen Post“ ist. Wer sich an den Pressekodex halte, sorgfältig arbeite und Persönlichkeitsrechte achte, habe einen Vertrauensvorschuss verdient.

### Presserat soll seine Arbeit sichtbarer machen

Dass der Presserat auch künftig gebraucht wird, steht für den früheren „Spiegel“-Chefredakteur Georg Mascolo ebenfalls außer Frage. Er wünscht sich allerdings, dass dessen Arbeit mehr Aufmerksamkeit bekommt. Die Entscheidungen des Gremiums sollten in der journalistischen Ausbildung und im Redaktionsalltag eine größere Rolle spielen. Außerdem forderte er, Lücken bei der Veröffentlichung öffentlicher Rügen im Internet zu schließen. „Schärfen Sie Ihr Regelwerk, und tun Sie es, wo immer es angemessen ist, und tun Sie es schnell.“

Auch Hamburgs Kultursenator Carsten Brosda hält die freiwillige Selbstkontrolle für unverzichtbar. Der Staat dürfe nicht darüber entscheiden, was guter oder schlechter Journalismus sei. Bei den großen Internetplattformen sieht er allerdings die Politik in der Pflicht: Sie müsse dafür sorgen, dass journalistische Angebote dort überhaupt eine Chance hätten, wahrgenommen zu werden. Brosda verwies dabei auf den geplanten Digitalen Medienstaatsvertrag, mit dem unter anderem die Auffindbarkeit journalistischer Inhalte verbessert werden soll.

On Nov. 24, 1947, the U.S. Navy launched the first Aerobee rocket into the sky, but it never reached space.

Aerobee was a suborbital sounding rocket designed to study Earth's atmosphere .

After World War 2, the United States started reusing erman V-2 rockets for this kind of research. When they started running out of V-2 rockets , the United States constructed its own rockets that were similar but cheaper to build and to launch. In the weeks leading up to the first Aerobee mission, three test flights were launched.

Those tests used a dummy version of Aerobee with a live booster to see if the two stages would separate properly. On Aerobee's first real flight, the rocket flew about 35 miles high. That's below the 62-mile (100 kilometers) upper limit for the boundary of space . (NASA and the U.S. military typically consider 50 miles the edge of space.) Mission control cut the flight short after about 30 seconds, because Aerobee started to yaw, and they wanted to keep it from going completely out of control.

## Why it mattered

Billed as the " most successful sounding rocket of the space age ," the initial Aerobee rocket was suborbital rocket designed to launch experment payload of up to 100 pounds (45 kilograms) to an altitude of 75 miles (121 kilometers) or so.

"The Aerobee was designed to carry instruments aloft to collect data on the upper atmosphere and to place small animals in a weightless condition for physiological studies," the U.S. National Museum of the United States Air Force wrote in a mission overview . "It was launched by a solid-propellant booster engine of 18,000 pounds thrust that burned for only two and a half seconds."

While the first Aerobee rocket did not reach space , many more made successful launches in the decades that followed.

Engineers made a steady stream of upgrades to the the Aerobee rocket, allowing to fly higher and launch heavier payloads into space. It was an Aerobee rocket that launched two Phillipine monkeys on a mission to study how the effects of rapid launch acceleration might affect their bodies, an experiment that was among the frst human physiology tests that paved the way for human spaceflight .

More than 1,000 Aerobee rockets have launched since then, and the last one flew in January of 1985.

As an editor with over 10 years of experience in science journalism she has previously written for Scholastic Classroom Magazines, MedPage Today and The Joint Institute for Computational Sciences at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. After studying physics at the University of Tennessee in her hometown of Knoxville, she earned her graduate degree in Science, Health and Environmental Reporting (SHERP) from New York University. Hanneke joined the Space.com team in 2016 as a staff writer and producer, covering topics including spaceflight and astronomy. She currently lives in Seattle, home of the Space Needle, with her cat and two snakes. In her spare time, Hanneke enjoys exploring the Rocky Mountains, basking in nature and looking for dark skies to gaze at the cosmos.

# Why a Case Against ICC Sanctions Is a Major Victory for Palestine Human Rights Work

A federal judge on Monday ruled that the Trump administration may not punish Americans for sharing evidence of Israeli war crimes with the International Criminal Court. The ruling also blocked the administration from meting out punishments for sharing information with three sanctioned Palestinian human rights groups and a prominent United Nations official.

The Monday ruling is the broadest challenge yet to an executive order issued by President Donald Trump in the early days of his second term that has been used by U.S. officials to issue sanctions against the ICC; the Palestinian groups al-Haq, al-Mezan, and the Palestinian Center for Human Rights; and U.N. special rapporteur Francesca Albanese.

> “It was kind of expected that they would make the preliminary injunction permanent, but the universal part is huge.”

The order, which came as a result of a lawsuit filed in July by Democracy for the Arab World Now, or DAWN, and the Taxpayer Alliance Against Genocide, is the latest setback to efforts by the Trump administration to undermine the efforts by the ICC, Albanese, and others to hold Israel accountable for crimes against humanity.

“This landmark ruling dismantles a core part of Trump’s ICC draconian sanctions regime,” said Omar Shakir, executive director at DAWN. “The court has affirmed that every American has the constitutional right to advocate for justice on Palestine without fear of reprisal.”

Most Read An Air Force Major Is Being Held in Solitary Confinement for Criticizing Trump on CNN Seth Stern ICE Spreads Misinformation About Securing Your iPhone. Here’s How to Really Do It. Noah Hurowitz, Nikita Mazurov, Karl Loftus Elon Musk Thinks You’re an Idiot Katherine Krueger

While previous rulings against Trump’s executive order applied more narrowly — including an October preliminary injunction in the ICC case that prevented punishments against the plaintiffs — this is the first ruling against the sanctions that protects all Americans.

“The main difference is that this was expanded to be universal, meaning it doesn’t just protect the people who filed the lawsuit in the first place,” Michael Schaeffer Omer-Man, the Israel-Palestine director for DAWN, told The Intercept. “It was kind of expected that they would make the preliminary injunction permanent, but the universal part is huge.”

## Related

### Trump’s Sanctions Against the ICC Are Unconstitutional, Rights Groups Say

A spokesperson for the White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment, but in a legal filing earlier this month, attorneys for Trump argued that his original executive order did not represent a restriction on free speech.

Another previous ruling that applied narrowly came in a case brought by a pair of university professors who challenged the administration’s prohibition on working with the ICC. Joseph Pace, a lawyer for DAWN and the Taxpayer Alliance Against Genocide, said this ruling also helped overcome some of the limitations in the professors’ successful case.

“It didn’t stop the administration from enforcing the sanctions against anyone else,” he said, of the decision in the professors’ case. “Nor did that decision say anything about the Palestinian NGOs or Albanese” — neither of which had been sanctioned yet at the time of the ruling.

“The permanent injunction, though, is what’s called a ‘universal injunction,’” Pace told The Intercept. “That means the government can’t penalize anyone for providing (or receiving) First Amendment-protected services to or from ICC, Albanese, and the NGOs.”

## “ Challenging These Crimes”

In his ruling, U.S. District Judge Jesse Furman found that the so-called services provision of Trump’s order — which threatened penalties for anyone “providing services” to the ICC, Albanese, or the three Palestinian NGOs — was unconstitutional because it undermined the First Amendment rights of people seeking to provide non-financial services to human rights advocates.

## Related

### Inside the Trump Administration’s War on the International Criminal Court

In a statement, Taxpayer Alliance Against Genocide co-founder Anna Marie Stenberg said the ruling by Furman provided immediate clearance for her organization and others to resume work with the ICC, Albanese, and the three Palestinian organizations.

“We challenged Trump’s Executive Order on the ICC because we refused to let his regime intimidate us into silence while it used our tax dollars to fund crimes against humanity,” Stenberg said. “This victory means that others can join us in challenging these crimes without fear of punishment for exercising their First Amendment rights. Ordinary people have a right to seek justice, and our government cannot take that right away.”

Trump’s Executive Order 14203, issued in February 2025, called for financial penalties against the ICC under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act. It barred Americans from providing financial assistance or services to further the court’s activities. Trump’s order explicitly cited the court’s investigations into Israel as a justification for the sanctions.

The order led to sanctions by the Trump administration against Albanese, who has consistently drawn the ire of pro-Israel officials for pursuing investigations into Israeli war crimes . The sanctions barred her from entry to the U.S. and froze her assets in the country. Albanese challenged the sanctions and a judge threw them out in May, but they were reinstated later that month.

items.body:
NASA announced Monday that NASA+ content has found its first theatrical home at The Greenbelt Cinema in Greenbelt, Maryland, expanding the agency’s reach across major viewing platforms and bringing space even closer to home.

“The National Aeronautics and Space Act of 1958 calls us to share our story of space exploration with the broadest possible audience, and our partners help us accomplish that,” said Rebecca Sirmons, general manager of NASA+ at the agency’s Headquarters in Washington. “Artemis II captured the imagination of the Artemis generation, but we are just getting started. With Artemis III on the horizon and our sights set on building humanity’s first Moon Base, this is only the beginning of our story being told, and we’ll continue sharing transparent, engaging content every step of the way.”

NASA and The Greenbelt Cinema will kick off their partnership with screenings of the NASA+ original documentary “The Europa Effect,” which follows NASA’s journey to investigate the science driving future exploration of Europa, Jupiter’s icy moon. Dates for screenings will be announced soon on NASA.gov.

Future programming may include other NASA+ original content, in-person live streaming events of NASA’s Artemis missions, including the first crewed mission to the Moon under the Artemis program, additional Europa content, and more. NASA+ also will remain available for free, with no ads, through the NASA app and on the agency’s [website](https://plus.nasa.gov/).

Earlier this year during its [Ignition](https://www.nasa.gov/ignition/) event, NASA outlined a bold path forward for the agency, including increasing the cadence of [Artemis](https://www.nasa.gov/artemis) missions to the lunar surface, and building the first [Moon Base](https://www.nasa.gov/moonbase), among other agency priorities. Partnerships like this one help NASA maximize engagement with communities around the world by making the agency’s missions and educational content available to viewers on their preferred devices and channels.

For more information about NASA missions, visit:

**https://www.nasa.gov**

# 19 rumors about insider trading, prediction markets we've investigated

For years, accusations of insider trading have targeted politicians and celebrities. But with the second administration of U.S. President Donald Trump coinciding with the rise of online prediction markets such as Polymarket and Kalshi, rumors have multiplied that the president and his inside circle have gambled using privileged information before it's public, a practice that has yet to be fully outlawed .

In November, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who admitted to several affairs , including one with a suspected Chinese spy, was removed by the company's board, then quickly reinstated. Trump said he intervened in Huang's favor .

This resulted in reports that Trump, who owns Nvidia shares , financially benefited from Huang's return. Some critics suspected Trump even traded on this information . This would constitute insider trading, which is illegal, according to the Securities and Exchange Commission .

items.body:
# Raising the stakes for enterprise networks with AI modernization

Sponsored

In partnership with Tata Communications

Enterprise networks are under severe strain. As companies rush to deploy artificial intelligence, the technology is quickly becoming the biggest source of demand on the network . Now, agentic AI is adding to the load. Tasks conducted by AI agents generate an estimated 450% more network traffic than the same tasks done by human workers.

As AI inference shifts from hyperscale training clouds—the huge centralized data centers where raw AI models ingest vast datasets and learn—to real-time, latency-sensitive applications, the need for on-premises or near-premises infrastructure grows. As a result, the gap between enterprise networks that are ready to support AI and those that are not is widening. As few as half of enterprises believe their current networks can handle AI’s bandwidth and latency demands, according to a recent study .

This report explores how treating network modernization as an on-going strategy rather than a one-off project can help organizations adapt in the face of disruption and uncertainty.

Key findings from the report include:

AI may force companies to shift from a cloud-first approach to routing workloads. Training AI requires server-to-server data center architectures, while inference calls for low-latency connectivity close to users. Enterprises may need to fundamentally reconsider their network architecture to meet these requirements.

AI inference is pushing infrastructure back on premises. Inference typically requires real-time processing and is sensitive to latency, making hosting such capabilities on distant hyperscale clouds neither economical nor practical. Inconsistent latency can lead to AI model failures, driving up queue wait times, saturating GPUs loads, and causing bottlenecks in data flows. Large enterprises may need on-premises or near-premises inference, which reverses years of cloud-first consolidation and forces new approaches to data center architecture, connectivity, and physical infrastructure.

AI workloads are stressing physical network capacity in unexpected ways. The traffic increase from agentic AI, combined with inference moving on-premises, is exposing bandwidth bottlenecks in legacy underlay infrastructure.

Network modernization is an ongoing project that requires a holistic approach, allowing companies to adapt with ease. A combination of strong architectural governance, reusable design templates, and retained internal expertise supports organizations in adapting to disruptive events without rebuilding their infrastructure from scratch each time. Such events could include mergers and acquisitions, changing vendors, or technology upgrades.

NaaS and AI-driven observability can improve efficiency and reduce complexity in network operations. Network-as-a-service (NaaS) and AI-driven observability can offer companies benefits like faster, more flexible provisioning and lower costs.

Data sovereignty and sovereign AI will create infrastructure challenges for global enterprises. Regulators worldwide are passing laws requiring data and AI processing to remain within national borders. This conflicts with how multinational companies currently operate, requiring the build-out of sovereign-capable infrastructure for each geography, which will require significant new investment and complicate operations.

items.title: Distinct trajectories and predictability of individual grouping patterns in dolphins link social ageing to longevity
items.subtitle: Meehan, Barbara Class, Shinichi Nakagawa, Meredith MacQueeney, Vivienne Foroughirad, Janet Mann, Celine H.
items.feedText: Recent work has unearthed strong relationships between ageing and average sociability. Clear patterns of decreases in average sociability are observed across taxa; many of these are sex-specific. Individuals, however, generally deviate from population averages, and discounting individual variance in behaviour could disguise mechanisms of adaptation, selection, and developmental stability. Using 40 years of behavioural data from Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins, we provide new insights into so…
items.body: Recent work has unearthed strong relationships between ageing and average sociability. Clear patterns of decreases in average sociability are observed across taxa; many of these are sex-specific. Individuals, however, generally deviate from population averages, and discounting individual variance in behaviour could disguise mechanisms of adaptation, selection, and developmental stability. Using 40 years of behavioural data from Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins, we provide new insights into social ageing. We achieve this by simultaneously measuring both mean (repeatability) and variance (predictability) in group size—a trait reflecting social interaction preference—across the population and throughout individual lifespans. Double hierarchical location-scale modelling reveals a multidimensional response; at both the population and individual level, the mean trait response (plasticity) and variance (malleability) of group size change with age. At a population level and for most individuals, average group size increases then declines in later life. This decline is more pronounced in males, though males are consistently in larger and more predictable groups than females at all life stages. Population predictability of group size increases throughout life, consistent with our prediction that social preferences strengthen with age. Individuals which are highly sociable are also highly predictable, and increased sociability and predictability both appear correlated with longevity. The positive correlation between increasing predictability and longevity leads us to hypothesise that individuals develop social competence by refining their social experiences. This process likely involves increasing social selectivity and optimising social choices to achieve a net fitness benefit. These findings provide novel insights into social ageing and illustrate how studying variance in social traits can capture processes of social competence, selectivity, and adaptation of social phenotypes occurring within an individual’s social environment.

items.subtitle: Huang ist zurück als Chef von Nvidia.
items.feedText: Nvidia-Chef Wie hoch ist der Preis für Huangs Rückkehr? Stand: 24.11.2026 • 21:17 Uhr Huang ist zurück als Chef von Nvidia. Doch die Krise ist nicht ausgestanden. Der US-Kongress fordert Antworten. Und auch für Trump könnte der Fall Konsequenzen haben.
items.body:
# Jensen Huang ist zurück - doch für Nvidia und Trump könnte die Krise gerade erst beginnen

Nvidia-Chef Wie hoch ist der Preis für Huangs Rückkehr? Stand: 24.11.2026 • 21:17 Uhr

Huang ist zurück als Chef von Nvidia. Doch die Krise ist nicht ausgestanden. Der US-Kongress fordert Antworten. Und auch für Trump könnte der Fall Konsequenzen haben.

Jensen Huang hat seinen Job zurück - wohl auch dank des US-Präsidenten Donald Trump. "Ich habe schlimme Fehler gemacht", sagte Huang in einem Livestream einen Tag nach seiner Rückkehr als Chef des Chipherstellers Nvidia. Es sei nicht akzeptabel, dass er den Verhaltenskodex des Unternehmens, an dem er selbst mitgeschrieben hatte, gebrochen habe. Er sei in Therapie, sagte der Manager.

Doch mit der Entschuldigung kehrt keinesfalls Ruhe ein - weder im Unternehmen, noch an der Börse und der US-Politik. Für viele - Demokraten und Republikaner - ist die Intervention Trumps ein Skandal und eine Bedrohung der nationalen Sicherheit.

Trump hatte sich zuvor damit gerühmt, sich für den Manager beim Nvidia-Verwaltungsrat eingesetzt zu haben. Der US-Präsident besitzt laut Medienberichten Aktien im Wert von mehreren Millionen US-Dollar .

Der designierte Mehrheitsführer der Demokraten im US-Kongress, Chuck Schumer, warf dem US-Präsidenten vor, "unsere nationale Sicherheit für seinen finanziellen Profit", zu verkaufen. Die Rückkehr von Huang stehe für "die unglaubliche Korruption und Schwäche" des Präsidenten, sagte auch Josh Shapiro, Gouverneur von Pennsylvania.

Schon jetzt zeichnet sich ab: Der Fall dürfte für die Demokraten zur Steilvorlage werden, um vor den Gefahren der Trump-Politik zu warnen.

24.11.2026

### Bis zu 15 Millionen Dollar mit Aktien Wie Trump an Huangs Rückkehr zu Nvidia verdiente

Die Rückkehr von Jensen Huang ließ den Nvidia-Aktienkurs in die Höhe schnellen. Auch Trump verdient daran. mehr

## Scharfe Kritik auch aus den eigenen Reihen

Doch auch einige Republikaner finden deutliche Worte. Viele fordern seit Langem einen härteren Kurs gegenüber China. Dass Huang ausgerechnet im Verdacht steht, eine außereheliche Affäre mit einer mutmaßlichen Spionin aus China geführt zu haben, sorgt für Entsetzen. Laut US-Geheimdienstberichten soll sie Kontakt zum chinesischen Ministerium für Staatssicherheit gehabt haben. Die New York Times berichtet zudem von Kontakten zu Rüstungsunternehmen.

Als "Versagen" der Bundesbürokratie bezeichnete etwa Republikaner Newt Gingrich den Fall. Der US-Kongress müsse die "Frage der nationalen Sicherheit von enormem Ausmaß" gründlich untersuchen.

Der republikanische Senator Tom Cotton sagte, er habe "die Regierung von Anfang an davor gewarnt, dass das kommunistische China unsere fortschrittlichsten Chips sowohl durch Schmuggel als auch durch Fernzugriff in die Hände bekommen könnte". Die Kontroverse um Nvidia und Megaspeed - der Firma der mutmaßlichen chinesischen Spionin Alice Huang - sei nur die Spitze des Eisbergs. Das Problem sei "keineswegs" gelöst, "nur weil Jensen Huang seinen Posten zurück hat".

Auch in Deutschland sorgt die Intervention Trumps für Verwunderung. Außenminister Johann Wadephul sagte auf die Frage, wie er auf die Nachrichten über Nvidia reagiert habe: "Es hat mich schockiert, um ehrlich zu sein." Er habe "gewisse Zweifel, ob dies ein sehr gutes Modell für die Zukunft ist", sagte der CDU-Politiker. Soweit er dies beurteilen könne, habe er "eine derartige politische Einflussnahme auf ein einzelnes Unternehmen noch nie erlebt oder wahrgenommen".

23.11.2026

### Nvidia nach Spionageskandal Huang kehrt zurück - wegen Trump?

Dieser Rücktritt war von kurzer Dauer: Jensen Huang soll zurück an die Spitze des US-Konzerns Nvidia. mehr

## Weitere Untersuchungen im Januar?

US-Präsident Trump hatte zuvor seine Einflussnahme verteidigt: Seine Regierung habe keinen Grund zu der Annahme, "dass Jensens Rückkehr zu Nvidia ein Risiko für die nationale Sicherheit darstellt". US-Generalstaatsanwalt Todd Blanche habe ihm persönlich bestätigt, die US-Regierung verfüge über keinerlei Beweise, dass sich Huang rechtswidrig verhalten habe.

Dabei sind die Ermittlungen offiziell nicht eingestellt. Staatsanwalt Blanche hat offenbar nur mit Trump gesprochen, nicht aber mit Nvidias Verwaltungsrat. Eine Anklage wegen Verletzung von Geheimhaltungspflichten oder Exportgesetzen ist damit noch nicht ausgeschlossen.

Der US-Kongress fordert ebenfalls weiterhin Aufklärung. Am 1. Dezember werden drei Ausschüsse des Repräsentantenhauses - der Sonderausschuss für China, der Geheimdienstausschuss und der Auswärtige Ausschuss - eine nicht-öffentliche Anhörung mit Huang durchführen.

Die Befragung soll unter anderem klären, inwiefern China Zugriff auf die modernsten Technologien von Nvidia erhalten hat. Es geht auch um die Frage, ob das Unternehmen dazu beigetragen haben könnte, dass leistungsstarke Nvidia-Chips trotz geltender US-Exportverbote nach China gelangt sind. Es ist nicht bekannt, ob Huang unter Eid aussagen muss.

Zwei Tage später soll der neue alte Nvidia-Chef öffentlich vor dem Bankenausschuss des Senats Rede und Antwort stehen. Im Januar werden die Demokraten die Mehrheit in beiden Kammern des Kongresses stellen. Sie könnten dann weitere Untersuchungen anstrengen.

24.11.2026

### Rückkehr von Nvidia-Chef "Nie dagewesenes Verwischen von Grenzen"

Eine Rückkehr von Jensen Huang an die Spitze des Chipherstellers Nvidia haben die Wenigsten erwartet. mehr

## Zwischen Börsenhype und Ermittlungsdruck

Auch Nvidia will die internen Untersuchungen - insbesondere mit Blick auf die Exporte ihrer Chips - fortsetzen. Ein Compliance-Chef werde zudem noch gesucht. Wirtschaftlich hat das Unternehmen von der Rückkehr des von vielen als "Genie" gefeierten Huangs profitiert - die Aktie legte zunächst um 33 Prozent zu.

items.body:
**Körperliche Aktivität oder gesunde Ernährung: Einer neuen Übersichtsarbeit zufolge ist Bewegung für ein langes Leben womöglich wichtiger als eine gesunde Kost. In vielen Studien war Bewegungsmangel mit einem deutlich höheren Sterberisiko verknüpft als ungesunde Kost. Doch auch wer viel Sport treibt, sollte seine Ernährung nicht vernachlässigen.**

**Phoenix (U.S.A.).** Viel Gemüse und Vollkornprodukte, wenig stark verarbeitete Lebensmittel und regelmäßige Bewegung gelten als Grundpfeiler eines gesunden Lebensstils. Denn sowohl die Qualität unserer Ernährung als auch unsere körperliche Aktivität spielen eine Rolle für das Risiko chronischer Erkrankungen und eines vorzeitigen Todes.

Doch welche dieser beiden Stellschrauben ist wichtiger? Gerade bei der Vorbeugung von Krankheiten stellt sich die Frage, in welchem Maße sich die Risiken eines ungesunden Lebensstils durch Veränderungen des jeweils anderen Faktors ausgleichen lassen.

### Ernährung und Bewegung im Vergleich

Dieser Frage sind nun zwei Wissenschaftler nachgegangen, darunter Prof. Glenn A. Gaesser von der Arizona State University (ASU). Für ihre narrative Übersichtsarbeit haben sie vor allem Metaanalysen und große Langzeitbeobachtungen ausgewertet, in denen der Lebensstil von Menschen mit ihrem Sterberisiko in Beziehung gesetzt wurde.

> „Im Grunde wollten wir Klarheit darüber schaffen, wie sich die Auswirkungen körperlicher Aktivität und der Ernährungsqualität auf die Gesundheit beziffern lassen“, erklärt Prof. Glenn A. Gaesser.

Neben dem Ausmaß der körperlichen Aktivität berücksichtigten die Wissenschaftler auch die sogenannte kardiorespiratorische Fitness. Sie beschreibt, wie gut der Körper bei körperlicher Belastung Sauerstoff aufnehmen, transportieren und nutzen kann.

### Bewegungsmangel wiegt schwerer

Die Auswertung ergab ein deutliches Gefälle: Je nach untersuchtem Ernährungsmuster oder Lebensmittel war eine besonders ungesunde Ernährung mit einem um drei bis 20 Prozent höheren Gesamtsterberisiko verbunden. Bei Menschen, die sich am wenigsten bewegten und besonders viel saßen, lag das zusätzliche Sterberisiko dagegen bei 46 bis rund 163 Prozent, jeweils verglichen mit den entsprechenden Referenzgruppen.

Auch beim Vergleich gesundheitsfördernder Verhaltensweisen zeigte sich ein ähnliches Muster. Je nach Studie ging eine hochwertige Ernährung mit einem um vier bis 23 Prozent niedrigeren Sterberisiko einher, eine hohe Ausdauerfitness dagegen mit einem um 41 bis 53 Prozent geringeren Risiko.

Schon relativ kleine Unterschiede in der körperlichen Aktivität scheinen dabei eine Rolle zu spielen. Ein Unterschied von rund 2.000 Schritten pro Tag war in den ausgewerteten Untersuchungen mit einem um 23 bis 49 Prozent geringeren Sterberisiko verbunden.

### Kann Sport ungesunde Kost ausgleichen?

Aufschlussreich sind auch Studien, in denen Ernährung und Bewegung bei denselben Personen erfasst wurden. Das geringste Sterberisiko hatten dabei meist Menschen, die sich sowohl gesund ernährten als auch körperlich aktiv oder fit waren. Doch bewegungsfreudige oder fitte Menschen mit weniger gesunder Kost schnitten vielfach besser ab als körperlich inaktive Menschen mit gesunder Ernährung.

Zu diesem Befund passen Kurzzeitexperimente, bei denen sich Versuchspersonen über ein bis zwei Wochen besonders ungesund ernährten. Regelmäßige Bewegung konnte dabei viele der negativen Auswirkungen auf den Stoffwechsel und die Blutgefäße abschwächen oder verhindern. Umgekehrt gibt es kaum Belege dafür, dass eine gesündere Ernährung die körperlichen Folgen von Inaktivität ähnlich gut abfedert.

### Beides bleibt wichtig

Allerdings lassen sich die Risikowerte aus den unterschiedlichen Studien nur bedingt miteinander vergleichen, weil Ernährung, körperliche Aktivität und Fitness nicht einheitlich erfasst wurden. Zudem beruhen die Zahlen überwiegend auf Beobachtungsdaten. Sie beweisen weder, dass zusätzliche Bewegung das Leben um einen bestimmten Zeitraum verlängert, noch dass Sport die langfristigen Folgen einer ungesunden Ernährung ausgleichen kann.

Die Wissenschaftler plädieren daher nicht dafür, auf gesunde Ernährung zu verzichten. Vielmehr sprechen ihre Ergebnisse dafür, körperlicher Aktivität und Ausdauerfitness bei der Gesundheitsvorsorge mehr Gewicht zu geben als bisher.

**Quellen:**

- Originalstudie im Fachmagazin [Mayo Clinic Proceedings](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0025619626188065), doi: 10.1016/j.mayocp.2026.10.010
- Offizielle Studienmitteilung von [Arizona State University](https://news.asu.edu/20261112-health-and-medicine-you-arent-just-what-you-eat) (ASU)
- Offizielle Studienmitteilung von [Kaiser Permanente](https://www.kp-scalresearch.org/physical-activity-may-matter-more-than-diet-for-longevity/)

items.body:
> Young adults in advanced economies have grown more pessimistic about their economic prospects in recent years. At the same time, gambling-like financial activities have proliferated. We link these trends through a Friedman-Savage (1948) motive: when life goals such as homeownership or marriage seem out of reach, individuals turn to financial gambles. We test this theory using an original survey combined with millions of linked records from Korea’s leading credit bureau, telecom provider, and credit card issuer. Consistent with the theory, individuals who place greater importance on hard-to-reach goals take more risk, and the form of risk they take varies systematically with their distance from those goals. Within individuals, cryptocurrency app usage rises during unemployment and falls after winning the right to purchase price-regulated housing through a lottery. A calibration shows how hard-to-reach goals lead households to act more aggressively on their beliefs, amplifying the consequences of overoptimism.

That is from [a new NBER working paper](https://www.nber.org/papers/w36010#fromrss) by [Costas Arkolakis](https://www.nber.org/people/costas_arkolakis), [Spencer Y. Kwon](https://www.nber.org/people/spencer_yongwook_kwon), [Dominic Russel](https://www.nber.org/people/dominic_russel), [Claire Shi](https://www.nber.org/people/claire_shi) & [Hyunjoo Yang](https://www.nber.org/people/hyunjoo_yang).

items.title: NEPA is not an environmental protection law
items.subtitle: Two civil engineers examine project data on the construction site of a railway bridge.
items.feedText:

items.body:
Stepping back from the specifics of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) debate, I want to make a larger point about the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) and its role in American public policy:

This law has “environmental” in its title, but in a critical respect it’s just not an environmental law at all.

Which is to say it does not set any kind of standards related to environmental quality. The Clean Air Act makes rules about air pollution. The Clean Water Act makes rules about water pollution. We could make stricter rules about microplastics or forever chemicals or something else. We also have parks and other kinds of wildlife and landscape conservation programs.

None of this is NEPA.

NEPA is a law that makes it harder to do certain classes of things by imposing various procedural requirements, and it creates a litigation attack surface for people who do not like these classes of things.

NEPA is entirely indifferent as to whether the proposed thing is good for the environment or bad for the environment. What’s more, unlike real environmental laws, NEPA does not govern private-sector economic activity. The key idea of NEPA is the “major federal action.” It burdens government activities relative to private-sector activities and it burdens “action” (doing something new) relative to the status quo.

If you want to cut taxes on business investment to encourage more data center construction, that’s not a federal action for NEPA purposes, even though common sense says that tax law is a very important facet of federal policy. Maintaining the regulatory status quo is not a federal action even if the status quo is bad for the environment. If you want to build a light rail line that’s partially financed with a Department of Transportation grant, that’s a federal action and you need to do your NEPA homework.

If requiring federal (but not private) actions (but not inactions) to meet a set of burdensome procedural requirements leads to better environmental outcomes than not doing this, that would have to be essentially by coincidence.

I think a lot of progressive analytical errors about the post-1970 history of the United States are downstream of not understanding this.

It’s not just that progressives overrate NEPA but that they have an essentially false narrative of why contemporary government is the way it is. There’s this view that something called “neoliberalism” happened and that now because of “neoliberalism,” all the Democrats do is hand out tax credits rather than being cool New Dealers who support a robust state. But guess what — a tax credit to buy electric cars is not a major federal action but a mass transit line is.

NEPA is not the only reason for the rise of what [Suzanne Mettler calls the “submerged state”](https://www.amazon.com/dp/0226521656?lv=shuf&channelId=500&plpRedirect=mhFallback) or what [Mike Konczal calls government by coupon](https://www.newamerica.org/insights/no-discount-comparing-the-public-option-to-the-coupon-welfare-state/), but it’s striking that progressives tend to neglect its existence while workaday bureaucrats are painfully aware of its relevance.

#### The bias toward inaction

When New York City was thinking about launching its congestion pricing program to reduce traffic in parts of Manhattan and raise revenue for mass transit, it was granted the grace of being allowed to comply with NEPA via an environmental assessment rather than the more burdensome environmental impact statement. That less burdensome document runs [868 pages](https://www.mta.info/document/93446) with a two-volume appendix. The first volume of the appendix has [1,966 pages](https://www.mta.info/document/93451) and the [second volume is 1,173 pages](https://www.mta.info/document/93456). Yes, that is 4,000 pages worth of environmental review under the *less* burdensome of the two NEPA tracks for a program that charges people money to drive cars and uses the revenue to fund mass transit.

The reason the report has to be so long is not because the question of whether this is bad for the environment is hard to answer.

[↗ slowboring.com](https://www.slowboring.com/p/nepa-is-not-an-environmental-protection)

SAARBRÜCKEN. **Es ist ein Wortungetüm, das neue «Startchancen- und Qualitätsentwicklungsgesetz» des Bundes. Die saarländische Bildungsministerin kritisiert jedoch etwas ganz anderes am sogenannten SC-QEG. Damit seht sie nicht alleine da.**

„Wir sind uns einig“: Christine Streichert-Clivot (SPD). Foto: MBK / Holger Kiefer

Der Bund will Kitas dauerhaft zu mehr Förderung verpflichten, seine finanzielle Beteiligung daran aber reduzieren und bis 2035 beenden. Das stößt bei den Ländern auf Widerstand – speziell auch beim Saarland und seiner Bildungsministerin Christine Streichert-Clivot (SPD): «Wir sind uns darin einig, dass es nur schwer miteinander vereinbar ist, Standards bundesweit festzulegen und sich dann aber Schritt für Schritt aus der Finanzierung herauszuziehen», sagte sie. Der Bundesrat habe deshalb den Vermittlungsausschuss zum neuen Startchancen- und Qualitätsentwicklungsgesetz (SC-QEG) angerufen. Das Saarland hatte dazu gemeinsam mit Berlin einen Antrag vorbereitet, den alle Länder unterstützten.

Neben einer dauerhaften Sicherung in Höhe der derzeit zwei Milliarden Euro gehe es vor allem darum, «im Sinne der Kinder eine gute und nachhaltige Lösung zu finden». Das gemeinsame Anliegen sei es, Kindern schon früh die Unterstützung zu geben, die sie brauchen.

## Frühe Sprachstandserhebung mit «Startklar Deutsch»

Gleichzeitig betonte Streichert-Clivot, dass man die Ziele des Gesetzes aus saarländischer Perspektive unterstütze, weil es darum gehe, Bildungsgerechtigkeit zu stärken. So solle der Fokus auf die Jüngsten in der Gesellschaft gelegt werden und auf die Voraussetzungen, mit denen Kinder in die Schule starten.

Mit seinem Programm «Startklar Deutsch» erprobe das Saarland dies bereits: Denn schon zwei Jahre vor der Einschulung werde der Sprachstand der Kinder erfasst und diese anschließend gezielt gefördert. Der Bundesbeitrag dafür solle jedoch 2035 enden. «Genau das wollen wir in der Vermittlung ändern», so die Ministerin. Auch ein Scheitern des Gesetzes hätte finanzielle Folgen: Dem Saarland würden jährlich rund 11 bis 17 Millionen Euro fehlen.

Zudem setzten sich die Länder für eine möglichst unbürokratische Umsetzung der Gesetzesvorgaben ein. Der Bund erwarte teilweise Angaben bis zur einzelnen Förderzeit eines Kindes – dies sei «auch in der Nachweiserbringung später mit erheblichem Dokumentationsaufwand verbunden», so die Ministerin.

Streichert-Clivot, die im Vermittlungsausschuss in der Arbeitsgruppe für die SPD-geführten Bundesländer den stellvertretenden Vorsitz habe, erwartet, dass das Gesetz «mit einiger Härte» diskutiert werde – wobei die Konfliktlinie weniger zwischen CDU, SPD und Grünen, sondern tatsächlich zwischen Bund und Ländern verlaufe. *News4teachers / mit Material der dpa*

> [Streit ums Geld: Bundesrat stoppt Gesetz zu verpflichtenden Sprachtests für Vierjährige](https://www.news4teachers.de/2026/11/streit-ums-geld-bundesrat-stoppt-gesetz-zu-verpflichtenden-sprachtests-fuer-vierjaehrige/)

items.body:
Today, the [Booker Prize Foundation](https://thebookerprizes.com/the-childrens-booker-prize) announced the “Great Eight” shortlist of titles for inaugural Children’s Booker Prize, which will be awarded annually beginning in 2027. The Children’s Booker is the latest off-shoot of the prestigious Booker Prize (most recently awarded to M. John Harrison’s [The End of Everything](http://bookshop.org/a/132/9798217438655)) and celebrates fiction for eight- to 12-year-olds, written in or translated into English and published in the UK or Ireland. The winner will take home £50,000 and the Booker Foundation will be donating at least 30,000 copies of the shortlisted books to children across the United Kingdom and Ireland.

“Any of these books stands comparison with any adult book, whatever the category, on its own terms,” said Frank Cottrell-Boyce, Chair of the Children’s Booker Prize 2027 judges, in the shortlist announcement. He, along with fellow judges Sanchita Basu De Sarkar and Lolly Adefope, narrowed down the shortlist from 89 submissions and will be joined for the final decision by four young people: Ibrahim (12), Lainey (12), Luna (8), and Myla (11).

Here’s the shortlist:

Guy Bass, illustrated by David Roberts, [The Worst Thing That Could Possibly Happen](http://bookshop.org/a/132/9781454975045)

Catherine Bruton, [Tadpole Summer](http://bookshop.org/a/132/9798887774466)

Eoin Colfer and Andrew Donkin, illustrated by Giovanni Rigano, [War](http://bookshop.org/a/132/9781464261251)

Iqbal Hussain, *The Night I Borrowed Time*

Liz Hyder, illustrated by Tom de Freston, The *Teller of Tall Tales*

Mikey Please, *The Rambler’s Curse*

Jessica Scott-Whyte, illustrated by Becka Moor, *Séamus Almost Famous*

Shaun Tan, [Hometown](http://bookshop.org/a/132/9781646146987)

The winner will be announced in a ceremony on February 2, 2027.

items.title: What Happens When Elders Share Their Stories
items.subtitle: When I moved from the San Francisco Bay Area to a small, rural town in Vermont, I wanted to find a way to contribute to the local community.

items.body:
When I moved from the San Francisco Bay Area to a small, rural town in Vermont, I wanted to find a way to contribute to the local community. Knowing there was a significant senior population here, I reached out to the town librarian with hopes of helping elders share their stories.

The local historical society took interest in this idea, which led to an exhibit at the 159-year-old Tunbridge World’s Fair, and a book series entitled *Folk Life: Tunbridge Oral Histories*. The first two print runs sold out. The second collection of stories has just been published, and people are already asking who will be featured in the third.

What is it about life stories that strikes such a universal chord? And why is it important—and even imperative—to share our stories with others? I interviewed oral historians, teachers, and a digital storyteller to discover more about why the age-old tradition of recording oral histories continues to make such a significant impact for individuals and communities.

## Fostering connections and reflection

Storytelling is, according to scientific research, a biological shortcut to human connection. [Uri Hasson](https://blog.ted.com/what-happens-in-the-brain-when-we-hear-stories-uri-hasson-at-ted2016/) and fellow researchers at Princeton University discovered that the brains of the storyteller and listener physically sync up while a story is being told, promoting social connection, trust, and empathy.

The more emotionally affecting the story is, the stronger this connection becomes. As emotions and tension rise, hormones are released, including oxytocin, the “bonding hormone”; dopamine, which sharpens focus; and cortisol, which promotes attention and alertness as conflicts in the story arise. These hormonal responses enhance both the listener’s memory and connection to the storyteller.

For Erin Barnaby, a digital storyteller and 11th-generation Tunbridge native, oral histories create a connection not only to people, but also time and place. “My dad recently sold his house to my uncle, a house that he built on land that my grandfather had given to him. I love to hear him tell stories about the shifting of the land, from sheep farms to dairy farms and the shift from open pastures to forests.”

Even when the subject matter might not be instantly relatable, the process of listening to another’s stories still creates a profound interpersonal connection. Esther Ehrlich, who worked at [UC Berkeley’s Oral History Center](https://www.lib.berkeley.edu/visit/bancroft/oral-history-center) for six years before launching an oral history business of her own, experienced this sense of connection firsthand:

> I was assigned an interview with a former medical malpractice insurance guy, which initially didn’t interest me at all. And then lo and behold, after interviewing this man, I found him absolutely fascinating. What I came to discover was that by the time we were done, or even partway in, I came to love every single person I interviewed. I would feel connected to them and them to me.

## Providing unique perspectives

From that biological and psychological basis, oral histories make a critical social contribution.

According to the [Oral History Association](https://oralhistory.org/), “oral history is the oldest type of historical inquiry, stemming from the oral traditions of myriad cultures across the globe, predating even the written word.” These personal stories expand upon the narratives of history books, allowing people from varied walks of life to share their unfiltered experiences and perspectives. Indeed, many works by trained historians rely on oral histories.

The founders of [Voice of Witness](https://voiceofwitness.org/), a nonprofit dedicated to advancing human rights by amplifying unheard voices, believe that oral history “can democratize history, contribute to narrative change, and illuminate issues and events in a profoundly powerful way.” Enabling individuals to safely share their stories opens people’s minds to fresh perspectives and vantage points.

While oral histories are limited to an individuals’ memories and are by nature subjective, they remain incredibly valuable in their ability to paint a portrait of time and place. Plus, their narrative-driven format brings history to life in a more memorable way than date- and fact-focused textbooks.

Helen Marks, a former history teacher who has spoken to thousands of students about her experience as a hidden child in Belgium during World War II, has observed that when a person shares their stories, it brings that part of history to life:

> I am among the few surviving hidden children who are willing and able to talk about their experiences in the Holocaust. Reading numbers on a page does not create the same impact as someone standing or sitting in front of you describing a moment that was frightening or was so foreign they didn’t know what to do.... I think that when you connect a face, no matter what the face looks like, you get a wholly different reaction than when you read a page full of facts.

## Leaving a legacy

Throughout the interviews I conducted for *Folk Life*, the importance of leaving a meaningful legacy was a common theme. “That’s the reason we share our stories,” says Marsha Higgins, a history teacher for nearly 40 years. “It makes us feel like we matter.”

Higgins taught students to create personal narratives from a young age. Decades later, former students still express their thanks for her guidance in teaching them the importance of recording their experiences.

“I encouraged students to write down things that happened to them. It’s helpful to know at the time, you’re creating chapters in your life, that your story is just as interesting as anybody else’s.”

Like Marks, Higgins grew up around immigrants from Europe. “And they all had stories,” she says. “Whenever we got together, somebody would tell me a story. How do you make conversation without one? It’s just so much a part of who we are.”

…

items.title: The neuroscience of dreaming: neural mechanisms, phenomenological characteristics, and proposed functions
items.subtitle: Dreaming is a unique conscious experience that occurs during sleep.
items.feedText: Although traditionally associated with rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, dreams also arise during non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep, although their frequency, vividness, and form vary systematically across sleep stages. This narrative review synthesizes current advances in the neural mechanisms, phenomenological characteristics, and proposed functions of dreaming. Regarding neural mechanisms, we compare classical theories, including the activation-synthesis and neuropsychological hypotheses, and highlight that d…
items.body: Dreaming is a unique conscious experience that occurs during sleep. Although traditionally associated with rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, dreams also arise during non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep, although their frequency, vividness, and form vary systematically across sleep stages. This narrative review synthesizes current advances in the neural mechanisms, phenomenological characteristics, and proposed functions of dreaming. Regarding neural mechanisms, we compare classical theories, including the activation-synthesis and neuropsychological hypotheses, and highlight that dream generation relies on coordinated activity across the brainstem, forebrain, and neuromodulatory systems, and is predicted by, and correlated with, local activity changes within the posterior cortical “hot zone” and forebrain dopaminergic regulation. Phenomenologically, REM and NREM dreams differ markedly in duration, vividness, bizarreness, social interaction, and emotional valence. Functionally, the evidence is strongest for a correlational association between dream content and emotion processing, but even here causal direction remains unresolved. Evidence for threat simulation is mixed and partly disconfirming under prospective designs; evidence for creativity enhancement and unconscious expression remains suggestive but non-causal. We therefore conclude that functional claims about dreaming currently rest on weaker evidence than mechanistic claims about sleep-state control, and we frame the functional section accordingly. We conclude by discussing the methodological challenges and future directions for dream research.

items.body:
# Pharma: Bayer stoppt Vermarktung von Bestseller-Medikament in Deutschland

Pharmawerk von Bayer in Wuppertal: Hier wurde das Mediakment Kerendia entwickelt. Foto: dpa Zusammenfassung Nutzen Sie komprimierte Kernaussagen für maximale Effizienz in Ihrem News-Alltag – verfügbar im H+ Standard Abo. Jetzt für 1 € testen Düsseldorf, Berlin. Die Bayer AG zieht Konsequenzen aus dem Sparkurs bei der Erstattung neuartiger Arzneien in Deutschland . Der Pharmakonzern kündigte am Dienstag an, sein neues Medikament Kerendia Mitte Dezember hierzulande vom Markt zu nehmen. Für das Mittel seien keine wirtschaftlich akzeptablen Erstattungsbeträge durch die Krankenkassen erreicht worden.

Erstmals reagiert damit ein Anbieter aus Deutschland auf den zunehmenden Streit um die Bezahlung von Arzneien durch die Krankenkassen. Bayer verbindet die Rücknahme mit einer scharfen Kritik am Drücken der Preise.

Dies werde dazu führen, dass immer mehr innovative Mittel aus den Forschungslaboren internationaler Pharmakonzerne nicht mehr in Deutschland zur Verfügung stehen werden, sagte Bayer-Cheflobbyist Matthias Berninger dem Handelsblatt.

items.body:
# Anti-Trans-Gesetz im US-Sport: Klagen und Chaos an Schulen

- Startseite
- Politik
## Republikanern fliegt ihr Anti-Trans-Gesetz im Jugendsport um die Ohren – Tausenden Mädchen droht Startverbot

Stand: 24.11.2026, 22:18 Uhr

Von: Lisa Mahnke

Kommentare Drucken Teilen

Nach einem Volksentscheid im US-Bundesstaat Washington herrscht im Schulsport Chaos: Ärzte und Lehrer klagen gegen ein Gesetz, das Trans-Mädchen ausschließen soll.

Im US-Bundesstaat Washington sorgt ein transfeindliches Gesetz für erhebliche Unruhe im Jugendsport. Anfang November stimmten 56 Prozent der Bürger bei einer Volksabstimmung für Geschlechtstests für die Teilnahme an weiblichen Schulsportgruppen. Verbände legten kurz darauf Klagen ein. Nun droht kurz vor Inkrafttreten das Chaos: Mit Beginn der Wintersaison stehen tausende Schülerinnen und deren Eltern vor massiven Hürden.

„Der Konsens: Chaos. Arztpraxen bemühen sich verzweifelt, Abläufe festzulegen, und die Familien wissen nicht genau, was sie benötigen“, fasste die KXLY-Nachrichtenchefin Melissa Luck die Situation auf der Onlineplattform X zusammen. Für viele Eltern sei aktuell unklar, ob sie einen zusätzlichen Arzttermin benötigen.

## Widerstand aus dem Gesundheitswesen: Ärzte und Pfleger fordern Pause

Gleichzeitig regt sich gegen das Gesetz massiver Widerstand aus dem Gesundheitswesen. Am 23. November reichte der Washingtoner Landesverband der Krankenpfleger (Washington State Nurses Association; WSNA) gemeinsam mit neun weiteren Berufsverbänden Klage gegen das Gesetz, auch genannt I-638, ein. Initiiert wurde das Verfahren laut The Seattle Times von der Landesärztekammer (Washington State Medical Association; WSMA). Die Mediziner fordern, das geplante Inkrafttreten der Initiative zu pausieren.

In der Klage wird bemängelt, dass „klare, evidenzbasierte klinische Standards“ in I-638 fehlten, was potenziell zu unnötigen oder unethischen Tests führen könnte. Dazu schaffe das Gesetz eine finanzielle Hürde für die Teilnahme am Sport, da sich Familien den Test womöglich zum Teil nicht leisten könnten. Die Forderung: Das geplante Inkrafttreten der Initiative am 3. Dezember zu pausieren.

„Ärzte brauchen Zeit und klare klinische Leitlinien, bevor von ihnen verlangt wird, etwas umzusetzen, das nach unserem medizinischen Urteil nicht Teil einer routinemäßigen sportmedizinischen Untersuchung ist“, sagte Dr. Matt Hollon, Präsident der WSMA, laut der Seattle Times in einem Interview. Auch Sorgen um Privatsphäre und Ethik müssten thematisiert werden, meint Hollon.

## Übersicht zu I-638: Das sieht das Gesetz für Mädchen-Schulsport in Washington vor

## Kritik an invasiven Tests und Kulturkampf: Scharfe Reaktionen auf Anti-Trans-Gesetz für US-Mädchensport

Eine weitere Klage gab es laut Axios auf Initiative des Landeslehrerverbands, der zivilgesellschaftlichen Organisation TransFamilies und Eltern von Schülern in Sportgruppen. Organisationen warnen besonders vor der konkreten Ausgestaltung des Geschlechtsnachweises. Laut der Initiative „No Hate in WA State“ sieht das Gesetz nicht vor, das Geschlecht schlicht über die Geburtsurkunde nachzuweisen.

Stattdessen sollen biologische Merkmale wie die Fortpflanzungsanatomie, ein genetisches Profil oder der Testosteronspiegel maßgeblich sein. Bürgerrechtler warnen, dass Schülerinnen damit zu invasiven Genitaluntersuchungen gezwungen werden könnten. In den USA gibt es schon länger Streit um das Thema, bei dem die Bundesregierung teils Ermittlungen an Schulen einleitete. In der Vergangenheit stieß Trump zudem immer wieder Einschränkungen für queere Rechte an.

Libby Watson, Kampagnenmanagerin von „No Hate in WA State“, kritisierte gegenüber dem Guardian , dass hier Kulturkampf auf dem Rücken von Kindern ausgetragen werde: „Das sind Spaltungsthemen, um uns zu trennen und zu beherrschen. Wohnkosten, Benzinpreise – das sind die wirklichen Probleme, die die Menschen gelöst sehen wollen.“ Es werde enormer Aufwand betrieben, um eine winzige Gruppe von trans Mädchen auszuschließen. Auch an anderer Stelle gerieten zuletzt Schutzvereinbarungen für Schüler unter Druck.

## Streit um Republikaner-Gesetz: Sportverband betont Neutralität – Verstoß gegen Verfassung möglich

Der Washingtoner Verband für schulübergreifende Aktivitäten (Washington Interscholastic Activities Association; WIAA) arbeite laut eigenen Aussagen schon vor dem Inkrafttreten am 3. Dezember an der Umsetzung. Laut dem WIAA könnten Schulen im Einzelfall entscheiden, die Geschlechterüberprüfung für Jungen- und Mädchensportgruppen einzuführen. Der WIAA sah davon ab, eine politische Positionierung abzugeben. „Der WIAA muss sich an das Landesrecht halten“, heißt es.

Tatsächlich betrifft das Verbot nach Angaben der Regionalzeitung The Columbian unmittelbar nur rund zehn trans Mädchen im gesamten Bundesstaat. „Wir räumen jedoch ein, dass es wahrscheinlich noch weitere Fälle gibt, von denen wir nichts wissen“, betonte der WIAA-Sprecher Sean Bessette. Kritiker warnen, dass auch Mädchen, die nicht gängigen Rollenbildern entsprechen oder besonders athletisch sind, ins Visier geraten könnten. „No Hate in WA State“ forderte, dass sich jedes Kind auf seinem Weg zu sich selbst unterstützt fühlen sollte – inklusive trans Kinder.

Zudem könnte das Gesetz gegen die Washingtoner Verfassung verstoßen, die Geschlechterdiskriminierung verbietet. Denn I-638 gilt ausschließlich für Mädchenteams. Jungen sind nicht betroffen. Obwohl das Gesetz in Washington offenbar mehrheitsfähig war, ist die Debatte noch lange nicht vorbei. Vorgesehen ist, dass das Gesetz am 3. Dezember in Kraft tritt. items.body:
# Kartoffeln wachsen in künstlichem Mondstaub – doch für Nasa-Mondbasen bleibt eine Hürde

## Kartoffeln aus dem Mondstaub: Studie zeigt Chancen und Hürden für künftige Mondbasen

Bewohnte Stationen im All lassen sich langfristig kaum allein per Frachtrakete von der Erde mit Essen versorgen. Vor Ort bietet die Mondoberfläche zwar reichlich lockeres Gestein, doch dem grauen Boden fehlen wichtige Nährstoffe für Nutzpflanzen.

Für spätere Mondstationen testen US-Forscher:innen im Labor, wie Kartoffelknollen in künstlichem Mondstaub mit Wurmkompost heranreifen. (Foto: Nasa/Aymeric Goyer/David Handy/Oregon State University)

Forscher:innen der Oregon State University haben nun Kartoffeln in künstlichem Mondboden bis zur Ernte gezüchtet. Die Ergebnisse sind in einer Studie im Fachmagazin npj Microgravity nachzulesen.

Erst bei einer Beimischung von 30 Prozent Wurmkompost erreichten die Pflanzen ähnliche Knollenerträge wie in fruchtbarem irdischem Ackerboden. Allerdings maßen die Wissenschaftler:innen in Knollen einzelner Versuchsgruppen leicht erhöhte Werte bestimmter Schwermetalle.

Die US-Raumfahrtbehörde Nasa hat die Versuche im Labor finanziert. Hintergrund ist das Artemis-Programm der Behörde, das längere Aufenthalte von Astronaut:innen auf dem Mond vorbereitet.

Projektleiter Aymeric Goyer ordnet die Ernte in einer Mitteilung der Hochschule als Zwischenschritt für eine künftige Nahrungsmittelproduktion im All ein. „Wir haben herausgefunden, dass Kartoffeln ihren gesamten Lebenszyklus in simuliertem Mondboden abschließen können, wenn dieser mit organischem Material ergänzt wird“, sagt Goyer.

## Warum purer Mondstaub für Kartoffeln schädlich ist

Fast die gesamte Mondoberfläche ist von einer trockenen Schicht aus zertrümmertem Gestein, Staub und scharfkantigen Glaspartikeln bedeckt, die Fachleute Mondregolith nennen. Über Milliarden Jahre haben winzige Meteoriteneinschläge und kosmische Strahlung dieses Material so fein zermahlen, dass spitze Körnchen Pflanzenwurzeln mechanisch aufscheuern können.
